Out-of-sample comparison of candidate supports

Source: R/crossval.R
mc_graph_cv.Rd

Splits the units into folds, fits the graph layer on the units outside each fold and scores it on the units inside it, which compares candidate supports without a penalty term and without scoring a support on the sample that chose it. The assignment of units to folds is random, so call set.seed() beforehand for a reproducible split.

Usage

mc_graph_cv(fit, supports = NULL, folds = 5L, workers = 1L)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_cv'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

supports

a named list of candidate supports, each a two-column matrix of edges (rows \((i,j)\), response indices) or NULL for the complete graph. The default, NULL, compares the complete graph (named "unstructured") with the support the fit carries (named "fitted"), when that one is sparse.

folds

integer number of folds, at least two and at most the number of units (default 5).

workers

number of parallel workers (default 1, sequential). The folds are formed in the parent before any dispatch, so a given seed yields the same split at any worker count.

x

an object of class "mcg_cv".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_cv": a list with per_fold, a data frame with one row per support and fold (columns support, fold, score, the held-out score, and npar, the number of free parameters of the support, which is the same in every fold); summary, a data frame with one row per support ordered by decreasing score (columns support, n_folds, the number of folds with a usable fit, npar, score, the mean over those folds, se, the standard deviation of the fold scores divided by the square root of their number, and delta, the difference from the best); failures, a data frame of the fits that failed (support, fold, error); and folds, n and supports (the names of the candidates). print returns its argument invisibly.

What is scored

The Gaussian working criterion of the residual layer, the scalar the information criteria of mc_compute_criterion are built from, evaluated on the held-out residuals under the covariance fitted on the rest and divided by the number of held-out units, $$-\tfrac12\bigl[R\log(2\pi)+\log|\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{train}}| +\mathrm{tr}(\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{train}}^{-1}\hat S_{\mathrm{test}})\bigr],$$ where \(R\) is the number of responses, \(\hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{train}}\) is the between-response covariance fitted to the sample covariance of the training residuals, and \(\hat S_{\mathrm{test}}\) is the covariance of the held-out residuals. Each covariance is centered at the mean of its own part and divided by the number of units in it. Larger is better. The scale is that of a log density per unit, so differences between supports are directly comparable and a difference of a given size means the same at any fold size.

What is held fixed

The first stage is not refitted: the split is of the stored Pearson residuals, so the comparison is between structures for the residual covariance and not between whole pipelines. That is the question the sparse against unstructured comparison asks, and it keeps every support scored on exactly the same residuals.

See also

mc_compute_criterion for the in-sample criteria, mc_graph_stepwise and mc_select_lambda for supports to compare.

Other information criteria: mc_compute_criterion(), mc_graph_ploglik()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 400
K <- diag(4) * 2
K[1, 2] <- K[2, 1] <- -0.7; K[3, 4] <- K[4, 3] <- -0.7
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 4), n) %*% chol(solve(K))
d <- data.frame(y1 = Y[, 1], y2 = Y[, 2], y3 = Y[, 3], y4 = Y[, 4],
                x = rnorm(n))
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x, y4 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
sel <- mc_graph_stepwise(f, criterion = "bic")
mc_graph_cv(f, supports = list(unstructured = NULL, selected = sel$edges))
#> Out-of-sample comparison of 2 supports (5 folds, n = 400)
#> Held-out working criterion per unit, larger is better.
#> 
#>        support n_folds npar  score      se    delta
#> 1     selected       5    6 -5.516 0.08428 0.000000
#> 2 unstructured       5   10 -5.519 0.08580 0.003232
# }
